opportunities.name: Plan city trip: flight + hotel + tour, then log to notes
opportunities.description: For a given destination and date range, search round-trip flights from Paris on Google Flights, search hotels on Booking.com, find a top tour on Viator, and save a one-line trip summary (flight, hotel, tour with prices) in Notes.
steps: On Google Flights, keep origin Paris and set 'Where to?' to {destination}; pick the city option from the suggestions
Open the Departure picker, go to the right month, click {depart_date} then {return_date}, click Done (and Search/Reload if needed)
Note the top/cheapest flight's airline and price
On Booking.com, dismiss the sign-in/cookie popups, type {destination} in 'Enter destination' and pick the city option
Open the date picker, select {depart_date} as check-in and {return_date} as check-out, click Search
Open the top result and note the hotel name and total price
On Viator, reject cookies, search '{tour_query}', skip the date picker, and open the first result; note its title and price
In Notes, type 'Trip {destination} {dates}: flight {airline} {price}, hotel {hotel} {price}, {tour_query}: {tour title} {price}' in 'New note' and press Enter

opportunities.name: Compare two PyPI packages and log the comparison
opportunities.description: Look up two Python packages on PyPI and their repositories to get version, release date, GitHub stars and license for each, then save a one-line 'A vs B' comparison in Notes.
steps: Click the PyPI search box, type {package_a} and press Enter
Open the exact-match result and note the version and release date
Click the 'Repository'/'Source' project link and note the stars and license
Repeat the search, open, and repository steps for {package_b}
In Notes, type '{a} {ver} {date} {stars} stars {license} vs {b} {ver} {date} {stars} stars {license}' in 'New note' and press Enter

opportunities.name: Answer a browser-support question by email
opportunities.description: Check a web feature's browser support on caniuse.com, find its MDN docs page, and draft an email reply to a colleague giving the minimum supported version for a specific browser plus the MDN link.
steps: On caniuse.com, clear the search box, type {feature} and press Enter; read the minimum supported version for {browser}
On MDN, click 'Search the site', type {feature}, press Enter, and open the matching reference page; copy its URL
In the mail compose form, enter {recipient_email} in To
Set Body to 'Hi {name}, {feature} is supported in {browser} from version {version}. Docs: {mdn_url}'
Send (in the recording the draft was discarded)
